environment: Windows 11 Pro; Node.js v24.19.0; Vitest 4.1.11; local tests/fake transports; no backend or staging connection.
method: For each representative invariant, save the exact dirty working-tree bytes, apply one temporary mutation, run only its owner test, record whether the intended assertion fails, restore the saved bytes in a finally-safe sequence, then compare SHA-256 before and after restoration.

mutations.invariant: A refresh result from an obsolete operation must not overwrite a newer logout or login session.
mutations.mutation: Changed the refresh success condition from operationId === operationRef.current to an unconditional applySession(session).
failedAssertions: ignores a late refresh success after a remote logout: expected true to be false
keeps a new login after remote logout when an older refresh succeeds: expected user-1 to be user-2
keeps a legacy synchronous login ahead of an older refresh response: expected user-1 to be user-2

mutations.invariant: Creating a watchlist item invalidates both the watchlist and pair-list queries that can become stale.
mutations.mutation: Removed pair-list invalidation from the watchlist-create mutation while retaining the watchlist invalidation.
mutations.targetedCommand: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --reporter=dot src/features/market/model/market-queries.test.tsx -t "invalidates the watchlist and pair list after creating a watchlist item"
mutations.failedAssertion: Expected invalidateQueries to include ['market','pairs']; it was not called with that query key.

mutations.invariant: A caller-supplied idempotency key remains on each retry so the server can deduplicate the logical mutation.
mutations.targetedCommand: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --reporter=dot src/shared/api/http-client.test.ts -t "keeps correlation and idempotency headers stable across retries"

limits: This is mutation sensitivity evidence for three selected frontend invariants, not a statement about mutation score across the repository.
Tests used local frontend fixtures/fakes and do not prove backend authorization, persistence, replay handling, staging behavior, or production readiness.
C03.05 still needs a fresh full-suite and coverage run; the WebLoginPage error-copy assertion mismatch remains unresolved pending product-intent evidence.
